content.title: About
content.content: Bass fillet (NFS) is a tender white meat from freshwater bass raised in controlled aquaculture conditions. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet flaky texture. The fillets are usually sold vacuum‑packed and ready for cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass is one of the most popular freshwater fish in Russia and the CIS countries.
In the wild bass can reach up to 1.5 kg, but farmed specimens are typically 300–500 g.
Bass meat contains very few bones, making it convenient for children and people with chewing difficulties.
Bass belongs to the Percidae family; its scientific name is *Perca fluviatilis*.
In Japan bass is often used for sushi and sashimi, while in Russia it is more commonly pan‑fried or baked.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Bass provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving contains about 20 g of complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium is a potent antioxidant and helps thyroid function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Makes bass suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bass.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Like other fish, bass can contain trace amounts of heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels may exacerbate gout symptoms.

items.title: Need for proper cooking
items.content: Raw bass fillet may harbor parasites; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bass fillet can be pan‑fried, baked, steamed, or poached in broth. For extra flavor, marinate in lemon juice, olive oil, and herbs for 15–30 minutes before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the fillet in its original vacuum pack in the refrigerator at +2…4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 2 months. Discard if it develops an ammonia‑like odor.
